detail:
MedlinePlus describes small bowel bacterial overgrowth as a condition in which very large numbers of bacteria grow in the small intestine, which normally does not have a large number of bacteria, unlike the large intestine. The excess bacteria may use up the nutrients needed by the body, so a person may become malnourished, and the breakdown of nutrients by the excess bacteria can also damage the lining of the small intestine and make it harder for the body to absorb nutrients. Conditions MedlinePlus lists as able to lead to overgrowth include complications of diseases or surgery that create pouches or blockages in the small intestine, diseases that lead to decreased movement of the small bowel, and surgical procedures that create a loop of small intestine where excess bacteria can grow.

MedlinePlus states that the goal is to treat the cause of the bacterial overgrowth. Treatment described includes antibiotics and medicines that speed intestinal movement. Nutritional support described includes intravenous fluids and, in a malnourished person, nutrition given through a vein, and MedlinePlus notes that a lactose-free diet can be helpful. The evaluation described includes blood tests for vitamin levels, and severe cases are described as leading to malnutrition, with other possible complications including problems due to vitamin deficiency and inflammation of the intestine.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about SIBO treatment and blind loop syndrome.
summary: MedlinePlus describes small bowel bacterial overgrowth management as treating the cause of the overgrowth, with antibiotics and medicines that speed intestinal movement, plus intravenous fluids and nutrition given through a vein in a malnourished person.
takeaways: treatment aims at the cause of the bacterial overgrowth
antibiotics and nutritional support are described treatments
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: SIBO: treating the cause of small bowel bacterial overgrowth
